_comment: First-run recipes. The 3 recipes without an origin are invented samples with full written methods. Used only when a new installation has no data file yet.

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Roast Chicken Traybake
recipes.ingredients: Chicken Thighs, Potato, Lemon, Garlic, Fresh Rosemary, Olive Oil, Salt, Black Pepper
recipes.notes:
Method (serves 4):
1. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
2. Cut the potatoes into 3 cm chunks and spread them on a large roasting tray.
3. Add the chicken thighs, skin side up, between the potatoes.
4. Crush the garlic cloves with the flat of a knife and tuck them in with the rosemary sprigs.
5. Halve the lemon, squeeze the juice over everything, then add the squeezed halves to the tray.
6. Drizzle with olive oil, season well with salt and black pepper, and toss the potatoes to coat.
7. Roast for 45 minutes, turning the potatoes halfway, until the chicken is golden and cooked through (75°C in the thickest part) and the potatoes are crisp.
8. Rest for 5 minutes and spoon the tray juices over before serving.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Salmon with Green Beans
recipes.ingredients: Salmon Fillets, Frozen Green Beans, Lemon, Soy Sauce, Honey, Garlic, Sesame Seeds
recipes.notes:
Method (serves 4):
1. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
2. Mix 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey, 1 crushed garlic clove and the juice of half the lemon in a small bowl.
3. Spread the green beans on the tray, add a splash of oil and a pinch of salt, and roast for 5 minutes.
4. Push the beans to the sides, lay the salmon fillets in the middle and brush them generously with the glaze.
5. Roast for 12–15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily.
6. Scatter the sesame seeds over the salmon, squeeze over the remaining lemon and serve straight from the tray.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Lamb Meatballs
recipes.ingredients: Lamb Mince, Feta, Fresh Mint, Onion, Passata, Cous Cous, Cumin
recipes.notes:
Method (serves 4):
1. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
2. Finely chop the onion and half the mint. Crumble half the feta.
3. In a bowl, mix the lamb mince, onion, chopped mint, crumbled feta, 1 tsp cumin, salt and pepper with your hands until just combined.
4. Roll into 16 walnut-sized meatballs and bake for 15 minutes.
5. Meanwhile, warm the passata in a wide pan with a pinch of salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
6. Add the baked meatballs to the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes more.
7. Pour boiling water over the couscous (1:1.25 by volume), cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
8. Serve the meatballs and sauce over the couscous, topped with the remaining feta and mint.
